name: CASE-Bench
description: Context-Aware Safety Benchmark integrates contextual information into safety assessments using Contextual Integrity theory (from privacy research). Unlike benchmarks evaluating isolated queries, CASE-Bench assigns formally described context (sender, recipient, setting, purpose) to each query, revealing that the same query can be appropriate or inappropriate depending on context. Commercial LLMs often fail to match human contextual safety judgments.
evaluation_method: contextual safety accuracy (agreement with human contextual safety judgments)
typical_sota_score: ~50–70% accuracy on contextual safety judgments (significantly below human agreement rates)
reputation: Published at ICML 2025; theoretically grounded in Contextual Integrity framework; addresses critical blind spot in context-free safety evaluation; reveals that context dramatically changes appropriate model behavior
notes: ICML 2025. Grounded in Contextual Integrity theory from Helen Nissenbaum's privacy framework — information appropriateness depends on social context norms. Finding: commercial LLMs 'often don't match human expectations' when queries are contextually appropriate but superficially look unsafe. For example, a nurse asking about medication overdoses should be treated differently than an anonymous user asking the same question. Addresses a fundamental limitation of context-free safety evaluation.
